- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the following 3–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% depending on sentiment decay.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) after a peak, model fails to adjust downward; force mean reversion toward 3–5 day average of prior 7–10 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; add 1–3% bias to forecast for next 5–10 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price by 1–4% when sentiment is stable or mildly positive; apply +1.5% bias to forecast if sentiment >0.5.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is falling, model overcorrects; reduce forecast by 3–6% to avoid “sell-off” overreaction.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts by 1–3 days; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change if sentiment is trending upward.
- When sentiment is high and price is near historical mean, model overestimates; apply 2–5% downward correction to avoid “overbought” bias.
